subject: Readout: vendor comparison anchors + agreed tests
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Readout: vendor comparison anchors + agreed tests

Thanks again for taking the time today — quick recap from our side and the concrete next steps we agreed on. I tried to distill the discussion into a short decision-playbook so your stakeholders can review quickly.

Pain & goals (as we heard):
- Reduce inference unit cost for clinician-facing summarization workflows (target: ~40% lower cost vs current provider)
- Keep median generation latency under 600ms for 512-token summaries
- Maintain or improve output quality (medical-entity recall / hallucination reduction)
- Platform requirements: VPC-only deployment, audit logs retained 1 year, SOC2 evidence for data-in-transit controls

Competitive anchors we discussed (quick comparison we sketched on the call):
- Vendor A (current incumbent): lowest latency in short bursts, poor caching behavior, limited quantization options
- Vendor B: strong batching and cost controls, but inconsistent entity preservation in clinical prompts
- Redwood (us): unified runtime with prefix/KV caching, model variants for cost/latency tradeoffs, rollout and fallback policies

Agreed tests for the bake-off / POC (actionable):
1) Latency & cost parity: run a 24-hour synthetic replay at your 50th/95th token-length distribution — measure median & p95 latency and per-1M-token cost.
2) Quality probes: 200-case blind set (mix of discharge notes and consults) to score entity recall and hallucination.
3) KV/prefix caching check: send sequences with large overlapping prefixes to measure cache hit rate and downstream latency improvement.
4) Failover behavior: simulate instance preemption to verify canary/fallback to regional replica without >1s client-observed stall.

Deliverables I attached: a compact comparison matrix (20270904_solano_comparison_matrix.xlsx) and a short POC scope doc (solano_poc_scope.pdf) that lay out the above tests and timeline.

Next steps (owners & ETA):
- Solano: pick 2 stakeholders to own quality acceptance criteria (Jessica/Tom, by Tue 9/7)
- Redwood (Karthik): provide POC runbook + simple script to replay traffic (by Mon 9/6)
- Redwood (Marissa): schedule the 60m technical kickoff and allocate initial GPU pool (by Mon 9/6)

If that aligns, we'll kick off the POC next week and drop in the test harness and credentials for the replay.

Thanks —
Aisha

Jessica — thanks, we'll prepare both the replay script and a SOC2/process excerpt. Quick tech notes so you know what we'll hand over with the runbook:
- Replay harness: Python script + docker image that can stream anonymized records into our hosted endpoint and your VPC connector. We'll include sample environment vars and an option to throttle to mimic your real qps.
- Latency measurement: we'll pass per-request timings and token-level breakdown (generation, KV lookup, scheduling).
- Cost model: conservative estimate using our quantization profile table (we'll include a spreadsheet).
- For the quality set: we'll accept your blind 200 cases as a CSV (we'll run them via a non-logged evaluation path and return only model outputs and the scored metrics).

Open questions we flagged internally (Karthik):
- Can Solano run the initial 2-hour replay in a staging VPC with VPN to our test endpoint, or do you need a hosted temporary endpoint behind your firewall?
- Are there any content-class restrictions in the dataset we should be aware of (PHI redaction you perform)?

I'll attach the runbook draft in our next release to the Drive link Aisha added.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Adding a short competitive readout I sketched after the call so we keep the decision criteria visible for the execs who will review:

Decision criteria (weighted):
- Quality (medical-entity recall / hallucination): 35%
- Latency (median & p95): 25%
- Total cost per 1M tokens: 20%
- Security & compliance (VPC, audit logs, SOC2): 15%
- Operational controls (rollouts, canary, autoscale): 5%

Initial observations from our internal benchmark vs public numbers:
- Vendor A: Quality 0.84 recall vs Redwood 0.87 on our clinical sample, median latency 420ms (good), poor caching (cache hit <5%).
- Vendor B: Cost profile competitive, recall 0.80, inconsistent on longer prompts (drops at 1k tokens).
- Redwood: recall 0.86–0.89 depending on model variant; our small-quantized variants show ~30–45% cost reduction in constrained memory configs.

Planned follow-up tests (owners):
- Karthik: share runbook + replay script (by Mon 9/6) — DONE, see Drive link.
- Marissa: allocate initial GPU pool + create a canary policy for preemption test (by Mon 9/6) — pending, please confirm.
- Jessica/Tom: confirm Dr. Patel & Lauren as quality owners (by Tue 9/7).

If there's no objection I'll lock the kickoff for Wed 9/8 10:00am PT and send an invite for a 60m technical kickoff (demo of replay, verification plan, data handoff checklist).

Thanks —
Aisha
